chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Ḥumayd ibn Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad al-Kindī, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the deceased who has hair upon him: should it be shaved from him or should it be trimmed? He said: “Nothing should be touched from him. Wash him and bury him.”

key_terms.اغْسِلْهُ: wash him with the prescribed ghusl for the dead
key_terms.الشَّعْرُ: hair on the body of the deceased
key_terms.لَا يُمَسُّ: it must not be touched or altered

ai.seo_question: Can the hair or nails of a deceased person be cut before burial in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the handling of the deceased before burial. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that no hair or nails are to be removed from the dead body; rather, the body is to be washed and buried as it is.
